title: England Must Chase Points Without Losing Discipline Against France
excerpt: After losing 30-12 to Tonga, England need big wins over France and Papua New Guinea — but Ashton and O'Neill warn the points will not come without discipline.
body:
• England face France in Perth on Saturday in their second Rugby League World Cup group fixture, after losing their opener 30-12 to Tonga.
  • England likely need big wins over France and Papua New Guinea, plus help from other results, to reach the semi-finals from the combined Pool B and C table.
  • Samoa's 78-4 defeat of France leaves England's points difference 92 worse than Samoa's, but winger Matty Ashton and hooker Brad O'Neill both warn against chasing points at the expense of discipline and execution.
  • Coach Brian McDermott has made one change: Ashton starts on the wing in place of Zach Eckersley, for his first World Cup appearance.

England go into Saturday's Rugby League World Cup match against France in Perth knowing a win alone may not be enough. After a 30-12 defeat by Tonga in their opening fixture, England need to win their remaining two group games and still require other results to fall their way to reach the semi-finals. Winger Matty Ashton, who comes into the side for the match, has stressed the need to balance the chase for points with retaining discipline, according to BBC Sport.

OVYScEH5TLQ

The Arithmetic England Face

The tournament format leaves England little room for error. Pools B and C form a combined six-team table from which only the top two advance to the semi-finals, and England, drawn in Pool B, play the three Pool C sides: Tonga, France and Papua New Guinea. Samoa's 78-4 win over France has left England's points difference 92 worse than Samoa's, so England must beat France on Saturday and then Papua New Guinea in Wollongong on Friday, October 30, and hope the rest of the table breaks in their favour. England have never failed to reach the semi-finals of a World Cup since the tournament began in 1954.

YzN-nj39UtY

Do Not Chase the Scoreboard

The temptation to run up a cricket score against France is obvious, and England's players have addressed it directly this week. Hooker Brad O'Neill, Super League's Man of Steel this year, told All Out Rugby League that England cannot afford to go into the game thinking about points difference.

"We've got to go into this game hard-nosed like we did against Tonga and hopefully if we do our jobs well enough, we're going to get the win, but we've got to treat them with the same respect as well."

— Brad O'Neill, England hooker

O'Neill said England's preparation would not change, and that the failure against Tonga was one of execution rather than approach. France, he noted, are familiar opponents through Catalans Dragons and Toulouse in Super League, and are coming off a defeat themselves. Ashton's message, reported by BBC Sport, makes the same point from the other side of the equation: the points England need will not come if discipline breaks down and penalties hand France territory and possession.

One Change From McDermott

Head coach Brian McDermott has resisted sweeping changes. The only alteration to the starting side is on the wing, where Warrington's Matty Ashton replaces Wigan's Zach Eckersley, as reported by Love Rugby League. McDermott said the switch was not a judgment on Eckersley's performance against Tonga, but a desire to look at other players; Ashton and Eckersley, he said, are similar types of player. Ashton was an unused substitute against Tonga and will now make his first World Cup appearance. Mikey Lewis has also been promoted to the bench.

McDermott pointed to the squad's disrupted preparation — two proper field sessions after a long journey to Perth — as a reason for confidence that cohesion will improve. England's tournament, and a semi-final place that has been a constant for more than 70 years, now depends on whether that improvement arrives on Saturday, with discipline intact and the scoreboard left to take care of itself.
